questions.question: The value of (1 - (1)/(2))(1 - (1)/(3))(1 - (1)/(4))(1 - (1)/(5)) dots dots dots (1 - (1)/(m)) is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For product series like (1 − 1/n), simplify the first 2-3 terms to identify the continuous cancellation pattern.

(1 − 1/2) × (1 − 1/3) × (1 − 1/4) ... = (1/2) × (2/3) × (3/4) ...

The numerator of each term exactly cancels the denominator of the previous term.

Remaining value = (Numerator of first term) ÷ (Denominator of last term) = 1 / m.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (1 − 1/2)(1 − 1/3)(1 − 1/4)(1 − 1/5) ... (1 − 1/m)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simplifying each bracket individually by taking the LCM.

⇒ Expression = [(2 − 1) / 2] × [(3 − 1) / 3] × [(4 − 1) / 4] × [(5 − 1) / 5] ... [(m − 1) / m]

⇒ Expression = (1/2) × (2/3) × (3/4) × (4/5) ... ((m − 1) / m)

⇒ Here, the denominator of each term gets continuously canceled by the numerator of the consecutive fraction.

⇒ Specifically, 2 cancels with 2, 3 with 3, 4 with 4, all the way up to (m − 1).

⇒ After complete cancellation across the entire series, only the numerator of the very first fraction and the denominator of the final fraction remain.

⇒ Result = 1 / m

**∴ The correct answer is 1/m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Telescoping Series

A series where intermediate terms cancel each other out, leaving only the initial and final terms. It frequently appears in fraction products and difference summations.

Addition Series Pattern

(1 + 1/2)(1 + 1/3)(1 + 1/4) ... (1 + 1/n) = (3/2) × (4/3) × (5/4) ... ((n+1)/n) = (n + 1) / 2.

Difference of Squares Series

(1 − 1/2²)(1 − 1/3²)(1 − 1/4²) ... (1 − 1/n²) = (n + 1) / 2n.
</p

questions.question: A dealer purchased a ceiling fan for ₹391. After allowing a discount of 31% on its marked price, he still gains 68%. Find the marked price of the ceiling fan.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula connecting Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP):

CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%)

391 / MP = (100 − 31) / (100 + 68)

391 / MP = 69 / 168 ⇒ 391 / MP = 23 / 56

MP = (391 × 56) ÷ 23 = 17 × 56 = 952

**∴ The correct answer is ₹952.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹391

Discount (D) = 31%

Profit (P) = 68%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100

 
 Marked Price vs Cost Price Relationship

 ₹952

 
 
•

•

 CP : MP = (100 − D%) : (100 + P%)
 391 : MP = 69 : 168

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Marked Price of the ceiling fan be MP.

⇒ SP in terms of CP = 391 × (100 + 68)% = 391 × 1.68

⇒ SP in terms of MP = MP × (100 − 31)% = MP × 0.69

⇒ Equating both Selling Prices:

⇒ MP × 0.69 = 391 × 1.68

⇒ MP = (391 × 1.68) ÷ 0.69

⇒ MP = 391 × (168 ÷ 69)

⇒ MP = 391 × (56 ÷ 23)

⇒ MP = 17 × 56 = 952

**∴ The correct answer is ₹952.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) and Discount

Discount is an allowance given to the buyer and is always calculated on the Marked Price (or List Price). SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Direct Relation between CP and MP

A very useful exam shortcut is the ratio CP : MP = (100 − D%) : (100 + P%). This allows you to find either value without calculating the exact Selling Price.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount can be found using the formula: Equivalent Discount = (a + b − a×b ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: A and B working together can do a piece of work in 3 days. B alone can do the same work in 12 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 3 and 12 = 12 units.

Combined efficiency of (A + B) = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 units/day.

Efficiency of B = 12 ÷ 12 = 1 unit/day.

Efficiency of A = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day.

Time for A to do double work (24 units) = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A and B together = 3 days

Time taken by B alone = 12 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Total Work = LCM of given days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A + B
 3
 12
 12 ÷ 3 = 4
 
 

 B
 12
 12 ÷ 12 = 1
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 4 − 1 = 3 units/day

⇒ Total work to be done = Double of original work = 2 × 12 = 24 units

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is similar to Time & Work. Filling pipes do positive work, while emptying pipes do negative work. Net efficiency = Sum of efficiencies of filling pipes − Sum of efficiencies of emptying pipes.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If workers operate for the same total duration, wages are divided strictly in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

When workers operate on alternate days, find the total work completed in one full cycle. Then divide the total work by the cycle work to determine the number of completed cycles and any remaining work.
</p

questions.question: Juli is 24 years older than her daughter. In 6 years, Juli’s age will be double that of her daughter. What is the present age (in years) of Juli?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The age difference between two individuals is always constant (24 years).

After 6 years, the ratio of Juli's age to her daughter's age will be 2 : 1.

Difference in ratio parts = 2 − 1 = 1 part = 24 years.

Juli's age after 6 years = 2 parts = 2 × 24 = 48 years.

Juli's present age = 48 − 6 = 42 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Juli is 24 years older than her daughter.

⇒ In 6 years, Juli's age will be double that of her daughter.

questions.question: The price of a commodity decreases by 5% in the first week and then increases by 8% in the second week. What is the effective percentage increase in the price after the second week?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For successive percentage changes, the effective percentage change is calculated using the formula: a + b + (a × b) / 100

Here, a = −5% (decrease) and b = +8% (increase).

Net % change = −5 + 8 + (−5 × 8) / 100

⇒ Net % change = 3 − 40 / 100 = 3 − 0.4 = +2.6%

Since the result is positive, it signifies an effective increase.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.6%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price decrease in the 1st week = 5%

Price increase in the 2ⁿd week = 8%

questions.question: A seller sells two fruits, apples and bananas. An apple costs ₹20 and a banana costs ₹10. Ravi buys 6 fruits and pays ₹80. How many more bananas did he buy than apples?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume all 6 fruits are bananas ⇒ cost = 6 × 10 = 60

Actual cost = 80 ⇒ extra = 20

Each apple costs 10 more than banana ⇒ number of apples = 20 ÷ 10 = 2

Bananas = 6 − 2 = 4

**∴ Difference = 4 − 2 = 2**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost of apple = 20, cost of banana = 10, total fruits = 6, total cost = 80

**Formula used:**

Form linear equations based on quantity and cost

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let apples = x, bananas = y

⇒ x + y = 6

⇒ 20x + 10y = 80

⇒ Divide second equation by 10 ⇒ 2x + y = 8

⇒ Subtract first equation ⇒ (2x + y) − (x + y) = 8 − 6

⇒ x = 2

⇒ y = 4

⇒ Difference = y − x = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Assumption Method

Assume all items are of cheaper type, then adjust using price difference.

Linear Equations

Use two equations: one for quantity and one for total cost.

Cost Difference Logic

Extra cost ÷ price difference gives number of costlier items.

questions.question: The average age of 30 students of a class is 19 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 20 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Age of new member = New Average + (Old Number of Members × Increase in Average)

Increase in Average = 20 − 19 = 1 year

Age of Teacher = 20 + (30 × 1) = 50 years

**∴ The correct answer is 50 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average age of 30 students = 19 years

Average age after including the teacher (31 people) = 20 years

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 
 
 

 
 

 
 
 30 Students (Avg = 19)
 Sum = 570
 
 
 
 
 30 Students
 Teacher
 Sum = 620
 
 
 
• 
 +50

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 30 students = 30 × 19 = 570 years

⇒ Total age of 31 people (students + teacher) = 31 × 20 = 620 years

⇒ Age of the teacher = Total age of 31 people − Total age of 30 students

⇒ Age of the teacher = 620 − 570 = 50 years

**∴ The correct answer is 50 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exclusion Method

When a person leaves the group: Age of leaving person = Old Average − (Change in Average × New number of people). Note that if the average decreases, the change is considered negative.

Replacement Method

When one person is replaced by another: Age of new person = Age of old person + (Total members × Increase in average).

Weighted Average

Used to find the combined average of two different groups: Combined Average = (N₁A₁ + N₂A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂), where N represents the number of items and A represents the average.

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 34 cm, 18 cm and 20 cm. What is the length of its altitude corresponding to the side with the length of 18 cm?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Semi-perimeter (s) = (34 + 18 + 20) ÷ 2 = 36 cm

Area = √(36 × 2 × 18 × 16) = 144 cm²

Altitude to 18 cm base = (2 × Area) ÷ Base

Altitude = (2 × 144) ÷ 18 = 16 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 16 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
• 
 C A B H 20 cm 18 cm 34 cm h = ? 

**Given:**

The sides of the triangle are a = 34 cm, b = 18 cm, and c = 20 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Heron's Formula for Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

Area of Triangle = 1/2 × base × altitude

**Calculations:**

⇒ Semi-perimeter s = (34 + 18 + 20)/2 = 36

⇒ Area = √[36 × (36−34) × (36−18) × (36−20)]

⇒ = √[36 × 2 × 18 × 16]

⇒ = √20736 = 144

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 18 × h

⇒ 144 = 9h

⇒ h = 16

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

Used to easily find the area of a scalene triangle when all three side lengths are explicitly known. Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)].

Area and Altitudes

A triangle has exactly three altitudes. The area of the triangle remains constant regardless of the base chosen: Area = 1/2 × b₁ × h₁ = 1/2 × b₂ × h₂ = 1/2 × b₃ × h₃.

Obtuse Triangle Altitudes

In an obtuse-angled triangle, the altitudes corresponding to the two shorter sides drop outside the main body of the triangle, intersecting the extended base lines.

questions.question: Given x + y = 4 , and xy = 2 , what is x² + y² ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Directly apply the algebraic identity: x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy

Substitute the given values x + y = 4 and xy = 2 into the expression:

x² + y² = (4)² − 2 × 2

x² + y² = 16 − 4 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + y = 4

xy = 2

**Formula Used:**

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

**Calculations:**

⇒ (4)² = x² + y² + 2 × (2)

⇒ 16 = x² + y² + 4

⇒ x² + y² = 16 − 4

⇒ x² + y² = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference of Squares

The difference of squares formula is x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y).

Square of a Difference

The formula is (x − y)² = x² + y² − 2xy. This helps find (x − y) when (x + y) and xy are known.

Sum of Cubes

The formula for sum of cubes is x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² − xy + y²).

Cube of a Sum

The formula for the cube of a sum is (x + y)³ = x³ + y³ + 3xy(x + y).
</p

questions.question: If 20% of 10% of 2/3 of a number is 697. Find the number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert all percentages into fractions and equate directly to the given value:

⇒ 20% = 1/5 and 10% = 1/10

⇒ (1/5) × (1/10) × (2/3) × Number = 697

⇒ (2/150) × Number = 697 ⇒ (1/75) × Number = 697

⇒ Number = 697 × 75 = 52275

**∴ The correct answer is 52275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

20% of 10% of 2/3 of a number is 697.

 N 
• 
 × 2/3 2N/3 
• 
 × 10% N/15 
• 
 × 20% N/75 = 697 Equivalent Operation: N × (2/3) × (1/10) × (1/5) = N / 75 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required number be N.

⇒ 20% of 10% of (2/3) of N = 697

⇒ (20/100) × (10/100) × (2/3) × N = 697

⇒ (1/5) × (1/10) × (2/3) × N = 697

⇒ 2 / (5 × 10 × 3) × N = 697

⇒ (2 / 150) × N = 697

⇒ (1 / 75) × N = 697

⇒ N = 697 × 75

⇒ N = 52275

**∴ The correct answer is 52275.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fractional Equivalents of Percentages

Converting percentages directly to fractions dramatically speeds up calculations. For example, 20% = 1/5, 10% = 1/10, 25% = 1/4, and 50% = 1/2.

BODMAS Rule in Simplification

The term "of" indicates multiplication but holds a higher precedence than standard division and multiplication as per the BODMAS rule (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

Successive Percentage Chaining

When finding sequential fractions or percentages (e.g., a% of b% of c), the values are simply multiplied in a chain. The operation is commutative, meaning changing the order of calculation does not change the result.

questions.question: In an election with two candidates, 8% of the registered voters did not vote, and 120 voters submitted blank ballots. Among the votes cast, the winning candidate received support from 48% of all registered voters and secured 780 more votes than the other candidate. Determine the total number of voters on the list.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total voters = x

Votes cast = 92% of x, valid votes = 0.92x − 120

Winner = 48% of x, loser = (0.92x − 120 − 0.48x)

Difference = 780 ⇒ 0.48x − (0.44x − 120) = 780

⇒ 0.04x + 120 = 780 ⇒ x = 16500

**∴ Answer = 16500**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

8% did not vote, 120 blank votes, winner got 48% of total voters, winning margin = 780

**Formula used:**

Total votes cast = 92% of total voters

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let total voters = x

⇒ Votes cast = 0.92x

⇒ Valid votes = 0.92x − 120

⇒ Winner votes = 0.48x

⇒ Loser votes = (0.92x − 120 − 0.48x) = 0.44x − 120

⇒ Difference = 0.48x − (0.44x − 120)

⇒ = 0.04x + 120

⇒ 0.04x + 120 = 780

⇒ 0.04x = 660

⇒ x = 16500

**∴ The correct answer is 16500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Vote Distribution Logic

Total voters include non-voters and blank votes, so adjust stepwise.

Percentage Conversion

Convert percentages into decimals for easier equation formation.

Margin Equation

Winning margin = winner votes − loser votes.

questions.question: The Rajdhani Express and Garib Rath Express run in the same direction with speeds of 87 km/hr and 51 km/hr, respectively, and their lengths are the same. What is the length of the Rajdhani Express if it completely crosses the Garib Rath Express in 175 seconds?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed = 87 − 51 = 36 km/hr = 10 m/s

Same length trains ⇒ total distance = 2L

Time = 175 sec ⇒ 2L = 10 × 175 = 1750

L = 1750 ÷ 2 = 875

**∴ Answer = 875 m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Rajdhani = 87 km/hr, Speed of Garib Rath = 51 km/hr, Time = 175 sec, lengths are equal

**Formula used:**

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed = 87 − 51 = 36 km/hr

⇒ Convert to m/s ⇒ 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

⇒ Total distance covered = 10 × 175 = 1750 m

⇒ Since both trains have equal length ⇒ total distance = 2L

⇒ 2L = 1750

⇒ L = 875 m

**∴ The correct answer is 875 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

Same direction ⇒ subtract speeds, opposite direction ⇒ add speeds.

Train Crossing Rule

Distance covered = sum of lengths when trains cross each other.

Speed Conversion

Multiply km/hr by 5/18 to convert into m/s.

questions.question: If P is a prime number, what is the HCF of P and P + 1 ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Any two consecutive integers are always co-prime to each other.

Since P and P + 1 are consecutive numbers, they share no common factors other than 1.

The condition that P is a prime number is extra information, as the HCF of any two consecutive numbers is always 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number = P (where P is a prime number)

Second number = P + 1

**Concept Used:**

If a number 'd' divides two numbers 'a' and 'b', then 'd' must also divide their difference (a − b).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of P and P + 1 be x.

⇒ This implies that x completely divides both P and P + 1.

⇒ By the property of divisibility, x must also divide the difference between the two numbers.

⇒ Difference = (P + 1) − P = 1

⇒ So, x must divide 1 completely.

⇒ The only positive integer that can divide 1 is 1.

⇒ Hence, x = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are defined as co-prime (or mutually prime) if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1. All consecutive integers fall into this category.

LCM of Co-prime Numbers

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) of any two co-prime numbers is simply the product of the two numbers. For example, the LCM of P and P + 1 is P × (P + 1) = P² + P.

Divisibility Rule of Difference

If an integer divides two numbers A and B (where A > B), it will also divide their difference A − B, as well as their sum A + B. This concept is the foundational basis of the Euclidean algorithm for finding HCF.
</p

questions.question: The amount on a sum of ₹2,500 at the rate of 14% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The effective compound interest rate for 2 years can be found using the successive percentage change formula.

⇒ Effective Rate = X + Y + (X × Y)/100

⇒ Effective Rate = 14 + 14 + (14 × 14)/100 = 28 + 1.96 = 29.96%

⇒ Total Amount = 129.96% of 2500

⇒ Total Amount = 1.2996 × 2500 = 3249

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,249.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Principal (P) = ₹2,500

Effective Compound Interest Rate

For 2 years at a rate of R% per annum, the effective compound interest rate is calculated using the successive percentage formula: [2R + R²/100]%.

Difference Between CI and SI

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for exactly 2 years on a principal P at rate R% is given directly by the formula: P(R/100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

When compound interest is calculated half-yearly, the annual interest rate is halved (R/2) and the number of compounding periods is doubled (2n).

questions.question: Simplify: sqrt{51 - sqrt{7 + sqrt{11 - 4sqrt{7}}}}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Start with the innermost square root: √(11 − 4√7) = √(√7 − 2)² = √7 − 2.

Substitute this value back into the intended expression: √(51 − √7 + √7 − 2).

The irrational terms −√7 and +√7 cancel each other out perfectly.

This simplifies the remaining expression to: √(51 − 2) = √49.

Finally, the square root of 49 is 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: √(51 − √7 + √(11 − 4√7))

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

**Calculation:**

⇒ First, evaluate the innermost radical: √(11 − 4√7)

⇒ The term inside can be rewritten as: 11 − 4√7 = 7 + 4 − 2 × 2 × √7

⇒ Applying the algebraic identity, we get: (√7)² + (2)² − 2 × √7 × 2

⇒ This perfectly forms a square: (√7 − 2)²

⇒ Therefore, the square root simplifies to: √(√7 − 2)² = √7 − 2

⇒ Now, substitute this result into the complete expression:

⇒ √(51 − √7 + √7 − 2)

⇒ The −√7 and +√7 terms offset and cancel each other out.

⇒ The expression now becomes: √(51 − 2)

⇒ √49

⇒ 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simplifying Surds of the Form √(a ± √b)

To simplify such surds, we convert the inner expression into a perfect square (x ± y)² = x² + y² ± 2xy, where the rational part equals x² + y² and the irrational part matches 2xy.

Addition and Subtraction of Surds

Only like surds (surds having the same index and same radicand) can be added or subtracted. For example, m√x ± n√x = (m ± n)√x.

Nested Radicals and BODMAS

When solving expressions with nested radicals, always begin simplification from the innermost radical and work your way outward step by step.
</p

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 87 cm, 108 cm, and 75 cm. What is the length (in cm) of its altitude corresponding to the side with a length of 108 cm?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify the side lengths by dividing by 3 to get a scaled triangle with sides 29, 36, and 25.

Semi-perimeter of scaled triangle, s = (29 + 36 + 25) ÷ 2 = 45.

Scaled Area = √(45 × 16 × 9 × 20) = √129600 = 360.

Scaled altitude on the base of 36 ⇒ 1/2 × 36 × h = 360 ⇒ h = 20.

Actual altitude = scaled altitude × 3 = 20 × 3 = 60 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 cm.**

**Given:**

Sides of the triangle are a = 87 cm, b = 108 cm, and c = 75 cm.

questions.question: ₹10,279 is divided among A, B, and C in such a way that if ₹67, ₹33, and ₹13 are deducted from their respective shares, they have money in the ratio 4 : 2 : 20. Find the difference between B’s and C’s original shares.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let reduced shares be 4x, 2x, 20x

Original shares ⇒ A = 4x + 67, B = 2x + 33, C = 20x + 13

Total = 10279 ⇒ 26x + 113 = 10279

x = 10166 ÷ 26 = 391

Difference = C − B = (20x + 13) − (2x + 33) = 18x − 20 = 7018

**∴ Answer = 7018**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = 10279; deductions: A = 67, B = 33, C = 13; ratio after deduction = 4 : 2 : 20

**Formula used:**

If quantities are in ratio a : b : c, then actual values = ax, bx, cx

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let reduced shares = 4x, 2x, 20x

⇒ Original shares: A = 4x + 67, B = 2x + 33, C = 20x + 13

⇒ Sum = (4x + 67) + (2x + 33) + (20x + 13) = 10279

⇒ 26x + 113 = 10279

⇒ 26x = 10166

⇒ x = 391

⇒ B = 2x + 33 = 815

⇒ C = 20x + 13 = 7833

⇒ Difference = 7833 − 815 = 7018

**∴ The correct answer is 7018.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Adjusted Ratio Method

When constants are added/subtracted, first assume ratio after adjustment, then revert back.

Linear Equation Formation

Form equation using total sum to find x.

Difference Shortcut

Difference can be directly computed as (ratio difference × x) adjusted by constants.

questions.question: If the Mode is 3 and it is given that the Mode is (3)/(2) times the Mean, find the square of the product of the Median and the Mean.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mode = 3 and Mode = (3/2) × Mean ⇒ Mean = 2

Use relation: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean

3 = 3 Median − 4 ⇒ Median = 7/3

Product = Mean × Median = 2 × (7/3) = 14/3

**∴ Square = 196/9 = 21(7)/(9) **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode = 3 and Mode = (3/2) × Mean

**Formula used:**

Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean

**Calculation:**

⇒ 3 = (3/2) × Mean

⇒ Mean = 2

⇒ Substitute in formula: 3 = 3 Median − 2 × 2

⇒ 3 = 3 Median − 4

⇒ 3 Median = 7

⇒ Median = 7/3

⇒ Product = Mean × Median = 2 × (7/3) = 14/3

⇒ Square = (14/3)² = 196/9 = 21(7)/(9) 

**∴ The correct answer is 21(7)/(9) .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relation

Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean (used for moderately skewed data)

Mean from Mode

If Mode = k × Mean, then Mean = Mode ÷ k

Square of Product

(ab)² = a²b²

questions.question: The angle of elevation of a ladder leaning against a wall is 60° and the foot of the ladder is 5.6 m away from the wall. Find the length of the ladder.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a 30°-60°-90° right-angled triangle, the ratio of the sides (Base : Perpendicular : Hypotenuse) with respect to 60° is 1 : √3 : 2.

The side adjacent to the 60° angle (base) corresponds to 1 ratio part.

The length of the ladder (hypotenuse) corresponds to 2 ratio parts.

Given 1 part = 5.6 m.

⇒ 2 parts = 2 × 5.6 = 11.2 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.2 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall (Base, CA) = 5.6 m

Angle of elevation at the foot of the ladder (θ) = 60°

**Formula Used:**

cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

Let the length of the ladder be L (Hypotenuse, AB).

⇒ cos 60° = CA ÷ AB

⇒ 1/2 = 5.6 ÷ L

⇒ L = 5.6 × 2

⇒ L = 11.2 m

**∴ The correct answer is 11.2 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios

sin θ = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse | cos θ = Base ÷ Hypotenuse | tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base.

Angle of Elevation vs Depression

Angle of elevation is formed when an observer looks upwards above the horizontal line of sight, whereas the angle of depression is formed when looking downwards below the horizontal line of sight.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is strictly equal to the sum of the squares of the remaining two sides: (Hypotenuse)² = (Base)² + (Perpendicular)².

questions.question:
An athletic track forms a shape consisting of a rectangle with semicircles on two opposite ends. If the straight portions are each 100 metres long and the total perimeter of the track is 400 metres, what is the radius of each semicircular end (rounded off to two decimal places)?

 (Use pi = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total track = 2 straight + 2 semicircles ⇒ 2 × 100 + 2πr

⇒ 200 + 2πr = 400

⇒ 2πr = 200 ⇒ πr = 100

⇒ r = 100 ÷ (22/7)

**∴ r = 31.82 m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of straight portion = 100

Total perimeter = 400

π = 22 ÷ 7

**Formula used:**

Total perimeter = 2 × length + circumference of circle

Circumference of circle = 2 × π × r

 
 
 100 m 100 m r 

Two semicircles form one full circle

Curved length = 2πr

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total perimeter = 2 × 100 + 2 × π × r

⇒ 400 = 200 + 2 × π × r

⇒ 2 × π × r = 200

⇒ π × r = 100

⇒ r = 100 ÷ (22 ÷ 7)

⇒ r = 100 × 7 ÷ 22

⇒ r = 700 ÷ 22

⇒ r ≈ 31.82

**∴ The correct answer is 31.82 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Track Shape Concept

Two semicircles together form one complete circle.

Perimeter Formula

Perimeter = straight parts + curved parts.

π Approximation

Use π = 22/7 unless specified otherwise.

questions.question: How many seconds will a boy take to run one complete round around a square field of side 25 metres, if he runs at a speed of 4 km/hr?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered in 1 complete round = 4 × 25 = 100 m

Speed in m/s = 4 × (5/18) = 10/9 m/s

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 100 ÷ (10/9) = 100 × (9/10) = 90 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 90 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of the square field = 25 m

Speed of the boy = 4 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a square = 4 × side

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance covered in 1 complete round = Perimeter of the square field

⇒ Distance = 4 × 25 = 100 m

⇒ Speed of the boy in m/s = 4 × (5/18) = 20/18 = 10/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken = Total Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time taken = 100 ÷ (10/9)

⇒ Time taken = (100 × 9) ÷ 10

⇒ Time taken = 900 ÷ 10 = 90 seconds

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed value by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply the speed value by 18/5.

Perimeter of Polygons

The distance around a closed geometric shape is its perimeter. For a regular polygon of 'n' equal sides, Perimeter = n × side.

Average Speed

It is defined as the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

questions.question: A fruit vendor buys 10 kg of apples at ₹85/kg and sells them at ₹100/kg. What is his total profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit per kg = Selling Price − Cost Price = 100 − 85 = ₹15

Total Profit = Profit per kg × Total quantity

Total Profit = 15 × 10 = ₹150

**∴ The correct answer is ₹150.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 

 
 CP: ₹85/kg

 
 SP: ₹100/kg

 

 Profit: ₹15/kg

 Total Quantity = 10 kg
 

 
 
 Total Profit: ₹150

**Given:**

Quantity of apples = 10 kg

Cost Price (CP) per kg = ₹85

Selling Price (SP) per kg = ₹100

**Formula Used:**

Total CP = CP per kg × Total Quantity

Total SP = SP per kg × Total Quantity

Total Profit = Total SP − Total CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP = 85 × 10 = ₹850

⇒ Total SP = 100 × 10 = ₹1000

⇒ Total Profit = 1000 − 850 = ₹150

**∴ The correct answer is ₹150.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit & Loss Percent

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the base of Cost Price (CP).

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount. The formula for discount percentage is Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer claims to sell goods at CP but uses faulty weights, his Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

questions.question: DMART is offering Buy 30, get 11 free on grocery items. What is the net percentage discount being offered by DMART? (Correct up to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In 'Buy X get Y free' offers, the discount is always calculated on the total number of items received.

Discount % = [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100

Total Items = 30 (paid) + 11 (free) = 41 items

Discount % = (11 ÷ 41) × 100 = 1100 ÷ 41 ≈ 26.83%

**∴ The correct answer is 26.83%.**
